classification.difficultyReason: The first task explicitly supplies the similar-triangle pairing and guides the side-length and area calculations. The second repeats that structure symbolically, requiring the remaining height x−y and a corresponding-side equation before comparing areas.

children.label: a
children.prompt: In the right-angled triangle $ABC$, there is a square $BDEF$, as shown.

spec.description: Right triangle with an inscribed corner square, vertex labels, two x cm labels and external full-side dimension arrows. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: AB=12 cm; BC=9 cm; angle ABC=90 degrees. D lies on AB, E on AC, F on BC; BDEF is a square.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are labelled; no calculated length is printed.

children.label: i
children.prompt: What is the abbreviated reason for $\triangle EFC$ to be similar to $\triangle ABC$?

answer.worked: $\angle EFC=\angle ABC=90^\circ$ and $\angle ECF=\angle ACB$ (common angle at $C$). Hence $\triangle EFC\sim\triangle ABC$ (AAA).

Since $BDEF$ is a square, $FC=9-x$. Matching sides of the similar triangles give
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{x}{12}&=\frac{9-x}{9}\\
9x&=108-12x\\
21x&=108\\
x&=\frac{36}{7}.
\end{align*}$$
The square's side length is $\dfrac{36}{7}\text{ cm}$.

children.label: iii
children.prompt: Hence, find the area of the square $BDEF$ as a fraction of the area of $\triangle ABC$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: In this diagram, square $BDEF$ is inside $\triangle ABC$, as shown. If $BC=x\text{ cm}$, $EF=y\text{ cm}$ and $AB=2BC$:

spec.description: Labelled right triangle and inscribed square, with a right-angle marker at B and no printed measurements. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: AB=2BC. D lies on AB, E on AC, F on BC; BDEF is a square.
spec.answerVisibility: No derived relationship or area ratio is shown.

answer.worked:
$\triangle EFC\sim\triangle ABC$ (AAA). Since $AB=2x$ and $FC=x-y$, matching sides give
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{y}{2x}&=\frac{x-y}{x}\\
y&=2(x-y)\\
3y&=2x\\
x&=\frac{3y}{2}.
\end{align*}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Hence, find the area of the square $BDEF$ as a fraction of the area of $\triangle ABC$.

answer.worked:
From part i, $y=\dfrac{2x}{3}$.
$$\begin{align*}
A_{BDEF}&=y^2=\frac{4x^2}{9}\\
A_{ABC}&=\frac12(2x)(x)=x^2\\
\frac{A_{BDEF}}{A_{ABC}}&=\frac{4x^2}{9}\div x^2\\
\frac{A_{BDEF}}{A_{ABC}}&=\frac49.
\end{align*}$$
